ImageDescription.value:
El presidente de la Junta de Andalucía, Juanma Moreno, ha acompañado esta tarde a Sus Majestades los Reyes, Don Felipe y Doña Letizia, en la entrega de los Premios Macael 2022, que coincide con el Encuentro Internacional de la Piedra, organizado por la Empresa Pública Andaluza de Promoción Exterior, Extenda. El Rey Don Felipe lucía en la solapa la Medalla de Honor de Andalucía que el presidente andaluz le hizo entrega el pasado año en un acto que tuvo lugar en el Palacio de San Telmo.

Estos Premios son un escaparate de la comarca del mármol y gran centro de referencia a nivel nacional e internacional de extracción, elaboración de proyectos especiales y comercialización de piedra natural y superficies compactas.

Esta nueva edición, que este año trae como novedad la inclusión de una nueva modalidad como es el Premio a la Sostenibilidad, supone una exhibición de buena salud del sector en Andalucía y también de sensibilidad y compromiso con los nuevos tiempos. También, son muestra de la fuerte apuesta por el uso de la tecnología, la labor de comercialización y la conquista de nuevos mercados, siendo todo ello su seña de identidad.

El Gobierno andaluz tiene un compromiso firme con este sector tal como lo demuestra el Plan de cadena de valor CRECE Industria de la piedra y el mármol en Andalucía aprobado el pasado mes de junio, que se enmarca dentro del Plan CRECE Industria 2021-2022, y que tiene asignada una dotación de 15 millones de euros y que conllevará la movilización de unos 63 millones de euros en inversiones.

Los galardonados este año en los Premios Macael son el arquitecto Luis Escarcena por el proyecto de reforma y remodelación del Hotel Silken El Pilar Andalucía y la Plaza de las Flores en Estepona (Málaga); el primer edificio residencial en altura de España con certificación Leed Gold, Torre Delfín en Benidorm (Alicante); Villa Dustin Bailey de MCA Systems en Dallas (Texas, EEUU), el Edificio Amot Holon de la ciudad de Holon (Israel), el Templo de Meditación de Málaga; la vivienda veraniega Villa Saba en Bali (Indonesia); el Ayuntamiento de Valencia por el proyecto de la Plaza de la Reina; la Residencia Villa Ricotta II en Marbella (Málaga); la restauración de la Iglesia de los Santos Mártires Ciriaco y Paula (Málaga) y el estudio de arquitectura Tobal Arquitectos de Marbella (Málaga). ————-

Fotografía oficial de la Junta de Andalucía, se pone a disposición solamente para su publicación por las organizaciones de noticias y/o para la impresión de uso personal por parte del sujeto (s) de la fotografía. La fotografía no puede ser manipulada de ninguna manera y no se puede utilizar en materiales comerciales o políticos, los anuncios, productos, promociones que de alguna manera sugieran aprobación o respaldo de la Junta de Andalucía.

ImageDescription.value: Former synagogue now adult library. Built in 1845. Late-classicist style. On the street front, is a Hungarian inscription: "egyedül az Istennek"=~"To God alone", on the courtyard side Hebrew inscription: presumably same is. At the top of the building are two Star of David. On its facade plaques one of these is the 'Plaque of Solidarity' inscription of its: ~"Let us remember our compatriots, known and unknown, who, in the dark days of 1944, bravely defended the Jewish citizens of the city with pity and compassion. /Erected by the Jewish Community of Baja with the support of Viktor Hegedűs in 2005"; the other facade plaque inscription: Pro Patria/To the glorious memory of our brothers and sisters of Baja who died heroically in the World War 1914-1918/(36 names, ranks, place names, years in two slops)/"It cannot be that so many hearts shed blood in vain......" - Inside is original the dual gallery system. The synagogue's built-in ritual artifacts, such as the vestibule's hand basin, the ornate bushing, and the Torah cabinet in the closet (there are 3 Torahs dedicated to the Five Books of Moses) have been restored.Some religious objects were also exhibited along with the parapet grid of the mizrah platform. - At the northwest wall of his garden there is an arcade where there is a Holocaust memorial, nearly a dozen memorial plaques. - At the northwest wall of his garden is an arcade where is a Holocaust memorial, nearly a dozen, memorial plaques (with names of victims). - 9 Munkácsy Mihály Street, Downtown, Baja, Bács-Kiskun County, Hungary.

ImageDescription.value: Photo taken of a computer screen at the start of 1980 text-adventure Zork.

Categories.value: Zork (game franchise)|Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy|Flickr images reviewed by FlickreviewR 2|The History of Adventure Games exhibition at PAX Prime 2011

ImageDescription.value:
Colossal Cave Adventure swept through colleges across country via the ARPAnet (the precursor to the Internet). By May, 1977, the game had been solved at MIT by a group called the Dynamic Modeling Group who believed that they could improve upon Colossal Cave. Working on a PDP-10 in MUDDLE (MDL), Dave Lebling wrote a command parser; Marc Blank, Bruce Daniels, and Tim Anderson worked on the design; and Blank and Anderson did the bulk of the coding. More sections of the map and puzzles were added over 1977-1979.

Infocom was incorporated in 1979 to be a commercial venture but with no fixed idea about what products would be developed. Selling Zork seemed like a good way to finance their future products. Joel Berez and Marc Blanc developed a virtual machine called the Z-machine Interpreter (ZIP) and the Zork Implementation Language (ZIL) that allowed Zork to run on a personal computer. The scaled down Zork was released for the TRS-80 Model I in 1980.

Infocom dominated the adventure genre for many years. Noted for rich language, imaginative plots and engaging characters, Infocom boasted that it relied on the world's best graphics processor - your brain. The graphics of the time were poor contenders. The demographics of computer owners (well educated and well-to-do) eliminated barriers to games that demanded a lot of reading. After an unsuccessful start with marketing by Personal Software, Inc., Infocom took over themselves, and they packaged the games with amusing extras that were sometimes essential to solving the game. Swamped by requests for help, they invented InvisiClues, booklets with invisible hints that were made visible by a special marker.

In 1982, work began on a relational database later named Cornerstone. A Business Division was formed, and the number of Infocom employees went from 32 to 100 to staff it. Game sales had slowed and the high-tech sector suffered a slowdown in 1985. Tensions developed between the game and business divisions, partly because the financial demands of Cornerstone left the game developers wihtout resources to innovate. Instead of the growth increase that had been expected to fund Cornerstone, revenues were stagnant. Competition from graphical games also impacted Infocom sales. In September, 1985, layoffs began; by the end of 1985, there were 40 employees left.

Cornerstone faced stiff competition in dBase, and although the product got excellent reviews, it did not capture a significant market share. In l986, Infocom merged with Activision. In 1989, Activision laid off more than half of Infocom's remaining employees and closed the Cambridge office. Only five of the remaining employees re-located. It was the end of Infocom and the Golden Age of the text adventure.
